item.text:
**6B.4 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**
Overall: **mostly no / mixed**
- There is real evidence of targeted, professionally delivered social-service activity, but the strongest positive items are mostly **partner-led** (World Bank, UNICEF, UNFPA, WHO) or **administrative reform** (procurement/delivery systems).
- I did **not** find strong direct evidence that Hasina’s rule broadly replaced patronage with meritocratic staffing across social services.
- The negative record is stronger on **politicization, corruption, and exclusion**, especially for Rohingya, minorities, and other vulnerable groups.

**Positive / partial evidence**
- **World Bank Helps Bangladesh Provide Basic Services, Opportunities, and Build Resilience for Displaced Rohingya and Host Communities** | World Bank | May 28, 2024 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/05/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-provide-basic-services-opportunities-and-build-resilience-for-displaced-rohingya-and-host-co)  
  - Claim: Bangladesh and the World Bank funded health, nutrition, family planning, child protection, WASH, and GBV services for Rohingya and host communities, with explicit attention to women and children.  
  - IDs: `6B.4`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **UNICEF, UNFPA and Canada partner with the Government of Bangladesh to improve access to essential healthcare services** | UNICEF Bangladesh | June 25, 2024 | [URL](https://www.unicef.org/bangladesh/en/press-releases/unicef-unfpa-and-canada-partner-government-bangladesh-improve-access-6-million)  
  - Claim: A five-year program aimed to strengthen primary health care for 6 million children and nearly 2 million women in underserved rural areas.  
  - IDs: `6B.4`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Bangladesh’s first national medical education strategy launched with WHO support** | WHO Bangladesh | March 4, 2024 | [URL](https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/04-03-2024-advancing-healthcare-excellence-who-s-role-in-developing-the-first-national-medical-education-strategy-in-bangladesh)  
  - Claim: The health ministry, with WHO support, launched a strategy to improve curriculum, accreditation, faculty development, and digital transformation in medical education.  
  - IDs: `6B.4`, also `6B.2`

- **UNFPA Bangladesh Annual Report 2024** | UNFPA Bangladesh | 2024 | [URL](https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/unfpa-bangladesh-annual-report-2024)  
  - Claim: UNFPA reported large-scale, technically delivered services for women, girls, adolescents, and persons with disabilities, including safe deliveries, GBV services, and cash assistance in crisis-affected areas.  
  - IDs: `6B.4`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Bangladesh - Cash Transfer Modernization Project: Improving Transparency and Efficiency of Safety Nets** | World Bank | January 1, 2024 | [URL](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099739201032424234)  
  - Claim: Bangladesh already had cash-transfer programs for the poorest and most socially excluded, including widows and older people; the project aimed to modernize delivery and improve transparency.  
  - IDs: `6B.4`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority public procurement reform / e-GP** | BPPA | July 24, 2024 | [URL](https://www.bppa.gov.bd/about-cptu/public-procurement-reform.html)  
  - Claim: BPPA said e-GP and e-PMIS improved transparency, efficiency, and competition in public procurement, with faster processing and more training for officials.  
  - IDs: `6B.4`  
  - Note: indirect evidence, but relevant because better procurement is a prerequisite for competent social-service management.

**Negative evidence**
- **Freedom in the World 2024: Bangladesh** | Freedom House | 2024 | [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024)  
  - Claim: Corruption was endemic, anticorruption enforcement was politicized, and minorities and refugees, especially Rohingya, faced discrimination and limited access to health care and education.  
  - IDs: `6B.4`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Bangladesh: Country Profile / Freedom House** | Freedom House | 2024/2026 profile page | [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh)  
  - Claim: The Awami League consolidated power through harassment of opponents and co-optation of state institutions, reinforcing a patronage-heavy governing style.  
  - IDs: `6B.4`

- **Macro Poverty Outlook for Bangladesh: October 2024** | World Bank | October 1, 2024 | [URL](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099659510152422672)  
  - Claim: Extreme poverty was projected to rise and inequality to widen by more than one Gini point, suggesting that social gains were not being broadly delivered in 2024.  
  - IDs: `6B.4`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Bangladesh crackdown / OHCHR statement** | UN OHCHR | July 26, 2024 | [URL](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights)  
  - Claim: More than 170 people were reported killed; some injured people were denied medical care; the UN said there was no effort to protect people from attacks by groups affiliated with the government.  
  - IDs: `6B.4`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Bangladesh repression / pre-election abuses** | Human Rights Watch | January 11, 2024 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections)  
  - Claim: Authorities arrested critics and used repression and violence before the election, indicating control politics was prioritized over neutral public service.  
  - IDs: `6B.4`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Fears grip ethnic minorities after deadly violence in Bangladesh** | Reuters | September 21, 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/fears-grip-ethnic-minorities-after-deadly-violence-in-bangladesh-3626672)  
  - Claim: Ethnic minorities in the Chittagong Hill Tracts were living in fear after clashes, with homes and businesses burned and families displaced despite heavy patrols.  
  - IDs: `6B.4`, also `6B.3`

**Search gap**
- I found **good evidence of service delivery** and **some evidence of administrative/procurement modernization**, but most positive items are either:
  - partnered with external agencies,
  - targeted to crisis-affected populations,
  - or limited to a technical subsystem like procurement or medical training.
- I did **not** find strong direct evidence that Hasina personally or systematically **broke patronage networks** in social-service staffing or governance in 2024.
- That gap matters: the available material supports **some competent delivery**, but not a clear, broad finding of **meritocratic social-service management**.
